ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of national patience
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("National Preferences and Student Achievement across Countries: The Intertwined Roles of Patience and Risk-taking"), column (3), row Patience.  Student-level least squares regression of the PISA math test score (original PISA scores divided by 100, so a unit is one standard deviation), pooled over all PISA waves 2000-2018, on the country's Global Preference Survey patience and risk-taking entered together.  Each preference is z-standardised in the analytical sample and collapsed to the country level. Controls: student gender, age and migration status, imputation dummies, and test-wave fixed effects.  Weighted by students' sampling probabilities within countries, giving equal weight to each country.  Sample: all students in the 49 PISA countries with GPS data.  Robust standard errors clustered at the country level.

ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of country-of-origin patience
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Patience, Risk-taking, and Student Achievement: Migrant Analysis"), column (3), row Patience (country-of-origin). Least squares regression of the PISA math score (divided by 100), PISA waves 2003-2018, on the GPS patience and risk-taking of the student's country of origin, entered together.  Sample: migrant students, both of whose parents were born outside the country where the student attends school, with an identified origin country that has GPS data.  First-generation migrants are assigned their country of birth, second-generation migrants their father's country of origin.  The sample spans 58 countries of origin and 48 residence countries.  Includes the 180 residence- country-by-wave fixed effects.  Controls: student gender, age, a dummy for an OECD country of origin, and imputation dummies. Robust standard errors clustered at the country-of-origin level.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Only the needed columns of the PISA files were read (data.table::fread select=); the replicate weights and other variables were skipped.

Table 1 (cols 1, 2, 3, 5) is estimated on an evenly spread block sample (about 20% of the rows, 0.5 MB blocks visited in van der Corput order until a 228 s time budget ran out) of Replication/Data/CSV/pisa_full_gps_final.csv. The full 3 GB file cannot be read through the read-only mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (measured raw throughput about 5-8 MB/s). All 49 countries and 253 of 263 country-waves are in the sample. Within each country-wave the sampled students' wgtc weights are rescaled to that cell's full weight (1/#waves of the country), keeping equal weight per country. The sample is timing-dependent, so a rerun can draw a slightly different subset.

table1_col3_observations is the observation count read from the <N> tag of the pisa_full_gps_final.dta header (1,992,276) times the complete-case share in the block sample (1.0); it is not the N of the sample regression. It is printed with %.6g as 1.99228e+06.

The preference measures are used as supplied in the data files (patience, risktaking, coo_* variables). These appear to be GPS measures z-standardised at the individual level in the analytical sample and then collapsed to the country level. They were not re-standardised across students.

Table 2 weights are the supplied student weight wgt (sampling weights normalised per residence country-wave), unchanged. Singletons are kept (fixef.rm='none'), so N = 80,398. Table 2 SEs are clustered by country of origin, Table 1 SEs by country.
deviations_stdout: Table 1 estimated on an evenly spread block sample of 19.9% of pisa_full_gps_final.csv (1180 of 5938 0.5 MB blocks, 395484 students) because the 3 GB file cannot be read through the mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (~6 MB/s); only the needed columns were parsed
table1_col3_observations is the row count in the .dta header (1992276) times the complete-case share in the block sample (1.00000); the sample regression itself used 395484 students
cell.notes: Table 1: weighted least squares of pv1math (PISA math / 100) on country patience and/or risk-taking with controls female, age, migration status (migra1, migra2), imputation dummies (imfemale, image, immigra0-2) and wave fixed effects. Weights are wgtc (equal weight per country); SEs are clustered by country. Natives (col 5) are students with migra1+migra2 < 1, and the migration dummies are dropped there. Table 2: migrant file pisa_full_gps_final_imcoo (80,398 students; 58 origin countries; 48 residence countries; 180 country-wave cells). Regressors are origin-country preferences plus female, age, OECD-origin dummy and imputation dummies, with residence country-by-wave fixed effects, wgt weights and SEs clustered by origin country. Claim attempt 1 (attempt-4) re-standardised the preferences across students and gave Table 2 equal weight per country; every coefficient was about 3x too small. Claim attempt 2 used the supplied variables and weights, and check_attempt then reported all claims within tolerance; that run is the final one, unchanged. Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (attempt 1 timed out while reading the full CSV; attempts 2-3 measured read speed and inspected variables).
